questions.question: Which of the following is a DML command in SQL?
questions.explanation: UPDATE modifies existing rows, so it is a Data Manipulation Language command. CREATE, ALTER and DROP change schema objects and belong to DDL.

questions.question: What does AJAX stand for?
questions.explanation: AJAX stands for Asynchronous JavaScript and XML, a technique for updating pages without a full reload. The other expansions are incorrect.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to create an instance of a class in most programming languages?
questions.explanation: In Java, C++, C# and JavaScript the new keyword creates an instance of a class. alloc is Objective-C specific.

questions.question: Which of the following is the type of Read Only Memory (ROM)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: PROM, EPROM and MROM (mask ROM) are all types of read-only memory, so more than one option is correct.

questions.question: When you drag selected text, you can
questions.explanation: Dragging selected text moves it to the new location (drag and drop). Copying requires holding Ctrl while dragging.

questions.question: The user IDs can be added or removed using which of the following fixed roles?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The db_accessadmin fixed database role can add or remove access for Windows logins, groups and SQL Server logins (user IDs). db_securityadmin manages permissions and role membership.

questions.question: In computer graphics, arrays can be used to store pixel values for images. Which type of array would be suitable for this purpose?
questions.explanation: An image is a grid of rows and columns of pixels, so a 2-D array maps naturally to it. A 1-D array loses the row/column structure.

questions.question: Who first used the term "IoT"?
questions.explanation: Kevin Ashton coined the term 'Internet of Things' in 1999 while working on RFID at Procter & Gamble / MIT Auto-ID Center.

questions.question: What is a segment base in segmentation?

options.A: The starting address of a segment in physical memory
options.B: The starting address of a segment in virtual memory
options.C: The ending address of a segment in physical memory
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In the segment table, the base holds the starting physical address of the segment, and the limit holds its length.

questions.question: Which one of the following computer networks is built on the top of another network?
questions.explanation: An overlay network is a virtual network built on top of another network (e.g. P2P networks over the internet).

questions.question: The minimum number of edges in a spanning tree of a connected graph with "n" vertices is:
questions.explanation: A spanning tree of a connected graph with n vertices is a tree on all n vertices, so it has exactly n - 1 edges. n(n-1)/2 is the edge count of a complete graph.

questions.question: Which of the following refers to the level of data abstraction that describes exactly how the data is actually stored?
questions.explanation: The physical (internal) level is the lowest level of abstraction and describes exactly how data is actually stored. The conceptual/logical level describes what data is stored, not how.

questions.question: File manipulation operations in an operating system include:

options.D: Reading, writing, and modifying file content

questions.explanation: File manipulation system calls include reading, writing and repositioning/modifying file content. Loading files into CPU registers or naming processes are not file operations.

questions.question: The popular method of organizing wireless network topologies is:
questions.explanation: Wireless (sensor and ad hoc) networks are commonly organized into clusters, each managed by a cluster head, to improve scalability and energy use. The other options are not topology organization methods.

questions.question: Which of the following options is not true about the binary search tree?

options.A: The value of the left child should be less than the root node.
options.B: The value of the right child should be greater than the root node.
options.C: The left and right subtrees should also be a binary search tree.

questions.explanation: All three statements are true properties of a BST (left smaller, right greater, subtrees also BSTs), so none of them is false.

questions.concept: read(n) and readline(n) file pointer movement
questions.question:
A text file song.txt contains the following contents in it:
Life goes on as it never ends
What will be the output of the following code snippet?
f1 = open("song.txt", "r")
s1 = f1.read(5)
s2 = f1.readline(4)
s3 = f1.read(3)
print(s1, s3, sep="#")
questions.explanation: read(5) returns 'Life ' (including the space), readline(4) reads the next 4 characters 'goes', and read(3) returns ' on'. Printing s1 and s3 with sep='#' gives 'Life # on'; s2 is read but not printed, so option B is wrong.

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Data members are bundled inside classes (encapsulation) and topper derives from student (inheritance). No overloading or overriding is shown, so polymorphism is not indicated.

questions.question:
The question below is an Assertion and Reason type question. Select the most suitable option considering the Assertion and Reason.
Assertion (A): When you enter a query into a search engine, it retrieves and presents a list of web pages, documents, images, videos, or other types of content that are relevant to your search.
Reason (R): The goal of information retrieval is to effectively and efficiently find and present information that matches the user's search criteria.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.explanation: A search engine returns relevant content for a query, and it does so because information retrieval aims to find and present information matching the user's criteria. Both are true and R explains A.

questions.question: Which of the following natural elements is the primary element in computer chips?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Computer chips (integrated circuits) are made primarily from silicon, a semiconductor.

questions.question: De Morgan's Theorems are particularly useful in simplifying logic expressions that have a large number of ___________.
questions.explanation: De Morgan's theorems let complemented sums and products be broken into simpler terms, which is most useful when an expression contains many terms. The theorems are not about simplifying constants or the number of operator types.

questions.question: All of the following are considered biometrics, except:
questions.explanation: Biometrics use physical or behavioural traits such as fingerprint, voice or retina. A password is something you know, not a biometric trait.

questions.question: Which among the following are the limiting factors of IoT?
questions.explanation: IoT devices are typically constrained by low power (battery), low processing power and low memory, so all of the above apply.

questions.question: The Cost Estimation technique that involves expert judgments and consensus is called:
questions.explanation: The Delphi method gathers estimates from several experts anonymously and iterates until consensus. COCOMO is an algorithmic model, while Waterfall and Prototype are life cycle models.

questions.question: The complement of a language will only be defined when and only when the _____ over the language is defined.
questions.explanation: The complement of L is Sigma* - L, so it can be defined only when the alphabet Sigma is specified.
